messages:
Maya: FYI customer ACME opened an escalation — Dedicated dashboard shows 6 GPU rows missing after the autoscaler replaced nodes in pool `worker-gpu-1` during the maintenance window. They say pools list has blank rows where GPUs used to be. Screenshot: https://redwood.screens/acme/missing_gpus.png

Jamie: Can you paste cluster + nodepool name and approximate time? Also any errors from inventory API or console?

Maya: Cluster: acme-prod-eu, nodepool: worker-gpu-1, approx: 2026-03-15T02:23:00Z when autoscaler replaced 3 nodes. Customer reported UI gap at 02:30. They grabbed these k8s snippets:

Maya: ```
$ kubectl get nodes -l topology.kubernetes.io/zone=eu-west-1 -o wide
NAME                      STATUS   ROLES    AGE   VERSION
ip-10-0-12-34.ec2.internal Ready    <none>   12d   v1.28.4
ip-10-0-12-35.ec2.internal NotReady <none>   1m    v1.28.4
```

Maya: and telemetry agent pod on one of the drained nodes shows crashloop:```
telemetry-agent logs:
E0315 02:22:34.123 inventory: failed to register node: 500 "no nodepool label matched selector"
```

Jamie: 500 from inventory service is notable — sounds like label selector mismatch after the node relabel. Did we deploy any selector/label changes recently? @Lina

Lina: I rolled out the inventory label-refactor on 2026-03-14 (small change to support `node_pool` snake_case var). The new config updates the selector from `nodepool` -> `node_pool` for some clusters via a feature flag. Looks like acme-prod-eu was included by mistake in the flag target. :grimacing:

Lina: Config snippet:
```yaml
inventory.selectors: ["node_pool", "poolName"]
# previously: ["nodepool", "poolName"]
```

Priya: That would break any telemetry agent that still reports `nodepool=` labels. Telemetry uses that label to group nodes -> pool rows. If nodes were drained/recreated without the new label key, inventory will drop them.

Jamie: Ok clear cause. Short-term options: 1) revert the feature-flag for acme-prod-eu, 2) run a resync job that maps existing `nodepool` labels to the new `node_pool` key, or 3) patch nodes to add `node_pool` label until node bootstrap picks it up.

Maya: Customer needs ETA. Which path is fastest?

Priya: Fastest: run cluster-side resync and restart the telemetry daemonset so agents re-register. Command I recommend (will run once approved):
```bash
# map node labels and trigger re-registration
kubectl get nodes -l "nodepool" -o name | xargs -I{} kubectl label --overwrite {} node_pool=$(kubectl get {} -o jsonpath='{.metadata.labels.nodepool}')
# then restart telemetry
kubectl rollout restart ds/telemetry-agent -n redwood-system
# trigger inventory resync
inventory-resync --cluster acme-prod-eu --nodepool worker-gpu-1
```

Jamie: I'll take lead on applying the label script + resync. Will coordinate with oncall to run during low load. I'll also push a rollback of the flag for acme-prod-eu if resync doesn't reconcile within 15m.

telemetry-bot: ALERT-30211 reindex job queued for acme-prod-eu (triggered by manual resync). ETA ~12m.

Maya: I'll tell ACME we have a remediation plan: running label sync + telemetry restart + inventory resync, ETA ~30m. Also offering them a temporary manual patch if they prefer immediate fix.

Lina: After this I will update feature flag targeting rules and add a canary check that verifies both `nodepool` and `node_pool` keys for 24h before wider rollout.

Jamie: Patch applied to 2 nodes as a quick test, resync started. Monitoring GPU rows in dashboard now.

Maya: Customer confirmed they see rows returning (partial). I'll keep them on the phone until full reconciliation. Thanks team :thumbsup:

Maya: I'll post a follow-up when everything is green.
